subject: barnstormerBiplane
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: barnstormer biplane.
Style: whimsical.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact biplane model with around 150 parts and a few textures, keeping it a static structure without joints since it's not an articulated vehicle, with a wingspan around 7 units.

I'm sketching out the construction plan: a lofted fuselage with red/cream paint, a lathed silver cowling, an extruded propeller with spinner, upper and lower wings with rounded tips and painted roundel decals, cabane struts and wires connecting them, plus a tail assembly with fin and stabilizers.

Now I'm adding wheels with hubs on a v-strut axle, a tail skid, a cockpit cutout with a pilot (head, goggles, streaming scarf), windshield, exhaust pipes and visible engine cylinders, and planning a "BARNSTORM" decal on both fuselage sides so the text reads correctly from outside.

I'm writing helper functions for boxes and rods, then placing the interplane struts and figuring out wing positions — upper wing around y=2.2 with cabane struts connecting down to the fuselage top near y=1.75, lower wing around y=1.0.

Now I'm defining the landing gear geometry with wheel hubs and struts connecting to the fuselage underside, then working out the fuselage loft cross-sections station by station from tail to nose, specifying width and height at each z-position to shape the cowling.

Still placing propeller geometry...

I'm planning a separate rudder, a box stabilizer with rounded elevator tips, and picking a whimsical color palette: red fuselage, cream stripes, blue accents, yellow wings. For the wings, I'm devising a custom paint function to add dark stripes along the ribs over the yellow base, plus capsule-style wingtip caps using cylinders aligned along the z-axis.

Now I'm adding a roundel decal on the upper wing with correct orientation, then placing a simple pilot figure with a spherical head and torso positioned in an open cockpit near the top of the fuselage.

Working out helmet, goggles, and a flowing scarf geometry—computing the cross product to keep the scarf flat and properly oriented in the side plane as it streams backward. Then I'm adding a tilted, semi-transparent windshield panel just ahead of the cockpit.

Now laying out the biplane's wing structure: upper and lower wing chord positions, interplane struts at specific x and z coordinates, and thin rods connecting the wings with crossed bracing wires for structural detail.

For the fuselage decal, I'm adding a cream-colored "FLYING PIE" text graphic with a dark outline, positioning it on each side of the body using mirrored placement so the text reads correctly from the viewer's perspective on both sides.

I'm painting the body with a procedural function: cream for the belly, blue near the tail, and red everywhere else, keyed off surface normal and z-position. Then I'm building out the wheels, hubs, landing gear axle, and V-shaped struts connecting the gear to the fuselage.
